title: Uniform tower tensor domain and evaluation of projection transposes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ of a scheme morphism $f=pj$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\ge1$. On each scheme $T$ use the varying-ring category $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of modules over $(A_{n,T})_n$ on the inverse-system pro-étale topos, its ordinary unbounded derived category, and its exact level evaluations [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Use the simultaneous derived section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for derived tensor over this ring system, exact termwise inverse image, exact termwise $j_!$, and derived direct image with its specified adjunction. Set $F=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ on bounded-below inputs [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels].

Let $C_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))$ and $B_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(Y,\mathcal O_E))$. Suppose there are integers $a\le b$ and $u\le v$, independent of $n$, such that $\mathcal H^i(C_n)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ and $B_n$ has Tor amplitude $[u,v]$, meaning $\mathcal H^i(B_n\otimes_{A_n}^LN)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $N$ and $i\notin[u,v]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Then $C_\bullet,B_\bullet,j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$ are bounded below, and both
$$C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet,\qquad j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet$$
have cohomology only in $[a+u,b+v]$. At every level this computation admits representatives $T_n$ for $C_n$ supported in $[a,b]$ and flat-term K-flat representatives $P_n$ for $B_n$ supported in $[u,v]$; the signed total tensors $T_n\otimes f^{-1}P_n$ and $j_!T_n\otimes p^{-1}P_n$ represent the evaluated derived tensors. Here flat means tensoring with a term is exact, and K-flat means total tensor with every acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. These level representatives are not required to form a strict tower.

The counit transpose under $p^{-1}\dashv Rp_{*,\bullet}$ and the unit transpose under $j_{!,\bullet}\dashv j^{-1}$ define actual derived tower maps, natural in both inputs,
$$\pi_p:FC_\bullet\otimes^LB_\bullet\to Rp_{*,\bullet}(j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet),\quad \pi_j:j_{!,\bullet}(C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet)\to j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet.$$
The transposes use the canonical pullback/tensor comparisons and respectively $\varepsilon\otimes1$ and $\eta\otimes1$. Their evaluations are exactly the corresponding finite proper and open projection maps, and $(Rp_{*,\bullet}\pi_j)_n=Rp_*((\pi_j)_n)$ under the canonical comparisons $(FD)_n\simeq Rp_*j_!D_n$ for $D=C_\bullet$ and $D=C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet$. No constructibility, normalization, or invertibility of these projection maps is asserted or required.

proof.text: Compare siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients with wfSiteDerivedTensor by restricting the published homotopy tensor descent comparison to the flat-term K-flat cochain representatives and applying cochain_tensor_model_rigidity. Transfer the Tor test along this natural isomorphism. Apply torAmplitude_iff_exists_bounded_flat_model to each B_n with the uniform interval [v,w]. A complex supported in that interval has vanishing homology outside it, so the representing isomorphism gives the bounds on B_n. The exact evaluation homology comparison and componentwise exactness detect zero tower homology, giving lower bounds on C and B; the exact open extension preserves the lower bound on C.

It returns a representative T_n strictly supported in [a,b] and an isomorphism C_n ≅ Q(T_n). Thus no separately imported truncation theorem or compatibility between levels is needed.

proof.text: Restrict the given level tensor model to flat-term K-flat representatives. The canonical pro-etale tensor pullback theorem makes the exact inverse images of P_n K-flat. The ringedTensorComparison_extension theorem computes tensor with any one K-flat factor for the actual prescribed level tensor. Compose this with tensorEvaluation, pullEvaluation and mapDerivedCategoryFactors to identify the first evaluated tensor with its signed total. Compose openEvaluation with exact open extension of the representing isomorphism to obtain the second identification. Exact inverse image and open extension preserve zero terms. For an out-of-range total degree every pair of summand indices has at least one zero factor; the total coproduct universal property makes the term zero. Transfer the resulting homology bounds along the representing isomorphisms and detect tower homology componentwise.

Use the existing maps_natural and properMap_evaluation laws of the tower compact-support projection interface. They are the recorded naturality and finite evaluation of the specified counit transpose, with the actual properMap unchanged.

proof.text: For openTensor inverse naturality, apply injectivity of the open derived adjunction homEquiv. Rewrite each adjunct by Operations.openTensor_mate. Naturality of the pullback tensor comparison and of the open adjunction unit identify the two resulting tensor morphisms. Use the existing openMap_evaluation law for the specified finite open transpose.

proof.text: Finally let \alpha_N:e_nGN\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*e_nN be the system lemma's natural direct-image comparison. Its naturality for the actual map \pi_j:JA\to JC_\bullet\otimes^LL says \alpha_{JC\otimes L}\circ e_nG(\pi_j)=Rp_*(e_n\pi_j)\circ\alpha_{JA}. This is the claimed equality (Rp_{*,\bullet}\pi_j)_n=Rp_*((\pi_j)_n) under the canonical comparisons. For D=C_\bullet and D=A, compose \alpha_{JD} with the exact open evaluation e_nJD=j_!D_n to obtain (FD)_n\simeq Rp_*j_!D_n. Step 1 and Step 4 put these two D in the stipulated bounded-below domain of F. All constructions were made before evaluation; no faithfulness of evaluations on morphisms or strict compatibility of the bounded level representatives is used.

Step 1: the flat-model lemma's condition (1) is exactly def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, so P_n lies in [u,v]. Exact evaluation and componentwise zero detection give bounds a and u, and exact j_! on systems gives bound a for j_!C. Step 2: τ≥aτ≤b with a qis roof; the a=b endpoint is H^a. Step 3: the finite column filtration argument for a bounded flat complex is correct and elementary. Advisory: it could have cited lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site (06YQ). Step 4: the pullback lemma applies because the constant-ring map is an isomorphism, so u^*=u^{-1}; the fixed-K-flat tensor allows a non-flat T_n; total degrees lie in [a+u,b+v]; system tensor evaluates to level tensor. Steps 5-6: both mate words have the right direction and match lem-coef's general projection transpose and open adjunction. Step 7: the naturality square of e_nG≅Rp_*e_n gives the equality. Advisory: these comparisons are lem-coef's, and the parent needs only invertibility. Edge cases checked: zero inputs, a=b, u=v, empty schemes, j=id. No SGA. Tool uses accepted: det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections and the two generic pbc K-flat/pullback tools. No new nodes, no fixes.
